title: Step through the model from inside
instruction: Three small programs that do the same as real AI, just on a small scale. Step through them line by line and answer what happens.

code: repeat until word is the name of a country:
candidates = words that follow word in the data
word = candidate with the highest probability

steps.input: Data: after “Vienna”: is 1.0 | after “is”: the 1.0 | after “the”: capital 0.67, second 0.33 | after “capital”: of 1.0 | after “of”: Czechia 0.67, Austria 0.33
steps.q: Which word does line 5 pick in the third round (after the word “the”)?
steps.why: “capital” has 0.67, more than “second” with 0.33. The model always takes the most likely one.

steps.q: Which word does the model pick now?
steps.why: In the data, “of” was followed twice by “Czechia” and only once by “Austria”. At this moment the model sees only the word “of”; it has already forgotten about Vienna.

options: Vienna is the capital of Austria
Vienna is the capital of Czechia
Vienna is the second largest city of Czechia
steps.why: Every step was likely, and yet the sentence is false. This is how a hallucination happens on a small scale.

steps.input: Go through the whole program once more
steps.q: On which line does the program check whether the sentence is true?
steps.why: No line checks the truth. The program only puts likely words together. Checking has to come from outside, from you or from a search.

code: for each example in the training data:

steps.input: New fruit: redness 2, diameter 7. First example: apple (9, 7)
steps.q: What does d come out as?

options: No, a pear is a different kind
steps.why: (2 − 3)² + (7 − 9)² = 1 + 4 = 5. That is less than 49, so the pear is the nearest so far.

options: No, d = 8 is not less than 5

steps.input: The fruit was actually a green apple
options: There’s a bug in the code
There was no green apple in the data
steps.why: The code calculates correctly. The mistake is in the data: green apples are missing from it. What isn’t in the data, the model can’t do.

code: show 4 videos in the ratio of the weights
for each video watched to the end:

steps.input: Round 1. You only watch videos about games to the end.
steps.q: How many videos about games will the feed show you in round 1?
steps.why: The weights are 1 : 1, so the 4 videos are split 2 and 2.

steps.input: Round 1: you watch both videos about games to the end
steps.q: What is the weight of games after round 1?
How many videos about science will you see in round 2?
steps.why: A ratio of 3 : 1 gives, out of 4 videos, 3 about games and only 1 about science.

steps.input: After round 2 you again watch only games to the end
steps.why: 3 + 3 = 6. Science didn’t get a chance, because the feed hardly shows it. That’s a feedback loop: what you see is what you click, and what you click is what you see.

debrief: Three programs, three lessons. A language model puts likely words together and doesn’t check the truth. Nearest neighbour calculates precisely, but only with what is in the data. And a recommender strengthens what it has already shown with every round.
